newsitem.title: FRANCE: Victor Hugo's descendants slam Disney film.
newsitem.headline: Victor Hugo's descendants slam Disney film.

text.p: Descendants of 19th century French writer Victor Hugo denounced Walt Disney Co's film "The Hunchback of Notre-Dame" on Monday, saying it amounted to "commercial pillage".
"We are profoundly shocked on several counts," five great-great grand-children of the novelist and poet said in an open letter published by the daily Liberation.

Charles, Adele, Jeanne, Sophie, and Leopoldine Hugo said that posters for the film, a box office hit in France based on Hugo's masterpiece "Notre-Dame de Paris", do not even mention the author's name.

And they wrote that a string of commercial spinoffs from the movie -- including cartoon books, electronic games, plastic models of the characters and advertisements in hamburger restaurants -- seemed "scandalous and obscene".

"Should not the cultural authorities of our country react against this commercial pillage of heritage and recall that the universality of a genius is something other than this vulgar globalisation by unscrupulous traders?" they asked.

"We believe that civilisation should guard itself against this pillage and the hijacking of great works of art to private commercial ends," they said. The Hugo family's rights to the work expired long ago.

The Disney movie departs from the plot of Hugo's work, about Quasimodo the unloved hunchback living in Notre-Dame cathedral in Paris. In the book, for instance, Quasimodo and the gypsy Esmeralda die but live on in the film.
